newsitem.title: UK: North Sea holds firm, tussle over Dated Brent.
newsitem.headline: North Sea holds firm, tussle over Dated Brent.

text.p: North Sea crudes held firm on Tuesday but the value of Dated Brent was unclear as cargoes traded at widely divergent levels in what traders said were attempts to benefit related swaps positions.
"There's clearly a two-tier market at the moment," said a trader.
"A major definitely wants the quote lower while others want it higher," said another.
A European major sold a Jan 8-10 Brent at Feb Brent +5 cents on Monday after another major sold a Jan 11-13 cargo at Feb Brent +15 cents.
There was unconfirmed talk that Monday's seller at Feb +5 cents sold another cargo, due to load Jan 9-11, for between Feb +5/+10 cents on Tuesday but this could not be confirmed.
Meanwhile, a U.S.-based trader recently clocked with a couple of cargoes offered Brent at Feb Brent +20 cents.
Feb Brent paper firmed notionally to $23.78 a barrel in line with stronger IPE futures after trading several times at $23.60 late in the U.S. on Monday.
Intermonth spreads were broadly steady with Jan/Feb talked at +34/+38 cents and Feb/Mar at +56/+60 cents.
Traders said other North Sea grades were very quiet.
On Brent CFDs, the balance of this week was bid at +12 cents and the Jan 6-10/Jan 13-17 roll was talked at +12 cents, up from +8 cents earlier.
No Brent cargoes were expected to turn wet on Tuesday, Shell UK having cancelled its Jan 15-17 equity cargo and Elf having moved its forward to the Jan 14-16 loading period.

In the Mediterranean, Russian Urals was on offer after the port of Novorossiisk reopened briefly on Monday, allowing two crude tankers to sail. The port shut again at 2240 local time but was expected to reopen later on Tuesday, shipping sources said.
